Following a wave of intensive real estate expansion in the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again growing its footprint in Sunnyvale. Here's the full story.

Apple continues to expand its business footprint

According to a report from The Mercury News (republished via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building located at 580 North Mary Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal marks the first major reported real estate move by Apple in the area in 2026; back in 2025, the company spent over US$1 billion expanding its presence in the South Bay.

That round of expansion included a US$166.9 million purchase of the three-building Cupertino Gateway complex, a US$350 million acquisition of the two-building Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale, and a US$365 million purchase of the adjacent four-building Mathilda Campus.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million on two buildings along Cupertino's Stevens Creek Boulevard, bringing its total Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Back to Apple's new lease — The Mercury News noted that the deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay has begun to pick up again, with vacancy rates improving both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year:

According to a Colliers report, the South Bay office vacancy rate stood at 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market as encompassing Santa Clara County and Fremont. The figure improved from the 14.8% vacancy rate recorded in the fourth quarter of October–December 2025, as well as the 16.2% vacancy rate in the second quarter of 2025.

Beyond Apple, the report also noted that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
